state.platform: Real ARM64 Home Assistant and OpenHarmony C ran in an independent ARM Linux VM. amd64 Home Assistant and the rebuilt C also ran under qemu-user. No independent native x86 host is available.
state.network: A manual AES-GCM client verified discovery, authenticated writes and actual virtual HA service audit/readback. Mac LAN-IP unicast used a private SSH/UDP relay. No external physical peer or Smart Life App LAN path was verified.
state.bug: The old C rejected a complete HTTP response when the server kept its connection open. The rebuilt C completed the same case without waiting for EOF and rejected truncated frames. The historical App failure had no transport reason recorded.
state.contribution: A separate branch contains public fan mappings, roles, device-native timers, composition and offline isolation; 52 tests and isolated HA Core checks pass. It excludes native engine integration and has not been pushed.
